description: An accordion is a vertical stack of collapsible sections that condenses long content into scannable headers.

paragraphs: An accordion is a vertical stack of collapsible sections that condenses long content into scannable headers.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: An accordion condenses long content into scannable headers. Users reveal one or more panels on demand — which also means content stays hidden until they open it.

sections.heading: Variants
paragraphs: Only one panel open at a time; opening one closes the others.
Any number of panels open independently.
Items separated only by spacing; no outline.
Single- vs multiple-expand is behavior (expandMode), not a Figma variant. Bordered and Borderless are the Style variant.

sections.heading: When to use
paragraphs: •   To condense long content into scannable headers that users open on demand.
•   For FAQ-style content, where users pick the questions they need.

sections.heading: When not to use
paragraphs: •   For content users must read in full.

sections.heading: Anatomy
paragraphs: •   ① Header — a heading element wrapping the trigger button; the whole row is the hit target.
•   ② Title — start-aligned label for the section.
•   ③ Icon — chevron showing collapsed or expanded; decorative.
•   ④ Content panel — revealed on expand.

sections.heading: Alignment
paragraphs: The title is start-aligned and the icon end-aligned on the same row. The trigger spans the full header width.

sections.heading: Placement
paragraphs: Items stack vertically at full width — never side by side. Spacing between items is consistent; borderless accordions rely on it as their only separator. Avoid nesting accordions; if you must, indent and limit to one level.
In single-expand mode, keep one panel open at a time.
Don't allow two panels expanded at once in single-expand mode.

sections.heading: Main elements
paragraphs: •   Wrapped in a heading (h2–h4) that fits the page outline.
•   Padding is tighter for text and roomier for complex content (contentType).
•   Every collapsed panel shows its icon, so hidden content always has a visible cue.

sections.heading: States
paragraphs: Items start collapsed (Default). Activating the trigger toggles its own panel; in single-expand mode, opening a panel collapses the one that was open.
•   Focused — 3px focus ring on the header; never suppressed.
•   Disabled — dimmed, can't change state, skipped in tab order.
See the Style tab for how each state looks.

sections.heading: Interactions
paragraphs: Clicking anywhere in the header toggles the panel.
Moves focus to the next trigger
Moves focus to the previous trigger
Moves focus to the first trigger
Moves focus to the last trigger
Disabled triggers are skipped. Full keyboard details are on the Accessibility tab.

sections.heading: Motion
paragraphs: Panels animate height and opacity (about 200ms, ease-out) and the chevron rotates 0° → 180° in sync. Only the active panel changes height — nothing above it reflows. With prefers-reduced-motion, toggling is instant.

sections.heading: Color
paragraphs: Swatches are bound to the live tokens.

sections.heading: Focus — zoomed
paragraphs: 3px ring bound to border/interactive/focus around the header.
An accordion is a vertical stack of collapsible sections that condenses long content into scannable headers.

sections.heading: What the design system provides
paragraphs: •   A Focused state with a 3px ring on the header, on both styles.
•   A chevron on every item, so collapsed panels always have a visible cue.
•   A Disabled state for triggers that can't change.
•   A full-width header, so the whole row is the hit target.

sections.heading: Development considerations
paragraphs: •   Wrap each trigger <button> in a heading (h2–h4). Never place the button outside the heading.
•   Set aria-expanded on the trigger and aria-controls pointing to its panel.
•   Give the panel role="region" and aria-labelledby pointing to the trigger; use the hidden attribute when collapsed.
•   Disabled triggers use disabled and are skipped in tab order.
•   Respect prefers-reduced-motion — remove height and rotation animation.

sections.heading: Keyboard interactions
paragraphs: Moves focus to the next trigger
Moves focus to the previous trigger
Moves focus to the first trigger
Moves focus to the last trigger

sections.heading: Design recommendations
paragraphs: Automated contrast check — WCAG 2.x relative luminance (sRGB), against the header or panel fill, for every theme combination. Minimums: 4.5:1 for title and body text, 3:1 for the icon, divider and focus ring, 3:1 for disabled text (house rule TKN-005). Note: project-a / light is measured against the current surface/bg/default, which resolves to blue because of the gray/50 token.
